Field manual-read route completion fell to 88% against a 95% target in that same window (E-01, 9200 accounts), triggering the meter-to-cash estimate-substitution step and producing estimated bills that account for the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills in E-02 — but not the larger 1785 ACTUAL-read disputed-bill share, whose cause current evidence does not establish.

VOB-U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-CAUSE.question: What causes the 1785 ACTUAL-read disputed bills (59% of disputes), since the estimate-substitution/route-completion mechanism does not apply to bills with an accepted actual read?

VOB-U-ROUTE-COMPLETION-ROOT-CAUSE.question: Is the claimed field-reader staffing shortfall (SH-FIELD, E-07) the actual driver of the route-completion shortfall in E-01, or is some other factor responsible?

interpretation_history.interpretation: Field route completion for manual-read accounts (9200 accounts) was 88% against a 95% target over Aug-Sep 2026, meaning roughly 7 percentage points of manual meter-read routes were not completed in the dispute-surge period, which the meter-to-cash process routes into estimate substitution when no accepted read exists.

Of disputed bills, 1785 (59%) carry an ACTUAL read and 1240 (41%) carry an ESTIMATED read, so a majority of disputes occur on bills that had an accepted meter read, not on estimate-substituted bills. This means theories tying the surge mainly to missing/failed reads feeding estimate substitution (AMI delivery, field-read handoff, or the estimate-substitution step itself) can at best explain the ESTIMATED subset and leave the larger ACTUAL-read share unexplained.

CRM response-time stats (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d, SLA 3.0d, 2440 tickets) show dispute tickets are being answered within SLA on aggregate, so the surge is not explained by slow/inadequate ticket response — undercutting the premise that an auto-answering AI agent addresses the surge's cause.

The billing-db tariff_change_log query returned zero records, meaning no tariff changes are logged in that system, which rules out a tariff/pricing change as a cause of the wrong bills or dispute surge.

The measured 88% manual-read route completion against a 95% target (9200 accounts, Aug-Sep 2026) still holds as a fact, but it no longer explains the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills: E-10 shows those bills are entirely AMI-channel records, not manual-read accounts, so route lateness/staffing does not feed this estimate-substitution pathway.

Of disputed bills, 1785 (59%) carry an ACTUAL read and 1240 (41%) carry an ESTIMATED read, so a majority of disputes occur on bills that had an accepted meter read, not on estimate-substituted bills. This means theories tying the surge mainly to missing/failed reads feeding estimate substitution (AMI delivery, field-read handoff, or the estimate-substitution step itself) can at best explain the ESTIMATED subset and leave the larger ACTUAL-read share unexplained.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Field route completion for manual-read accounts (9200 accounts) was 88% against a 95% target over Aug-Sep 2026, meaning roughly 7 percentage points of manual meter-read routes were not completed in the dispute-surge period, which the meter-to-cash process routes into estimate substitution when no accepted read exists.

The measured 88% manual-read route completion against a 95% target (9200 accounts, Aug-Sep 2026) still holds as a fact, but it no longer explains the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills: E-10 shows those bills are entirely AMI-channel records, not manual-read accounts, so route lateness/staffing does not feed this estimate-substitution pathway.

Of disputed bills, 1785 (59%) carry an ACTUAL read and 1240 (41%) carry an ESTIMATED read, so a majority of disputes occur on bills that had an accepted meter read, not on estimate-substituted bills. This means theories tying the surge mainly to missing/failed reads feeding estimate substitution (AMI delivery, field-read handoff, or the estimate-substitution step itself) can at best explain the ESTIMATED subset and leave the larger ACTUAL-read share unexplained.

The 1240 ESTIMATED vs 1785 ACTUAL disputed-bill split still holds and still shows the majority of disputes carry an ACTUAL read, unexplained by any estimate-substitution theory; E-10 further shows the ESTIMATED subset itself is entirely AMI-channel and dominated by billing-import high-consumption rejections, so field-read-handoff/staffing-lateness is no longer a viable explanation even for that minority subset.

CRM response-time stats (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d, SLA 3.0d, 2440 tickets) show dispute tickets are being answered within SLA on aggregate, so the surge is not explained by slow/inadequate ticket response — undercutting the premise that an auto-answering AI agent addresses the surge's cause.

The billing-db tariff_change_log query returned zero records, meaning no tariff changes are logged in that system, which rules out a tariff/pricing change as a cause of the wrong bills or dispute surge.

crm-tickets.dispute_volume_monthly (E-05) shows monthly dispute counts of 610 (2026-06), 590 (2026-07), 1180 (2026-08), 1260 (2026-09): volume roughly doubles from the Jun-Jul baseline (~600/mo) to the Aug-Sep period (~1200/mo), confirming the surge's magnitude and August onset timing but saying nothing about its cause.

E-10 breaks down the 1240 disputed ESTIMATED-read bills (matching E-02's total exactly) and shows they are entirely AMI read-channel records: 1184 (95.5%) had an AMI read received before cutoff and exported to billing but rejected by billing import as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, while only 56 (4.5%) had no AMI read received at all. This points to billing-import rejection of valid AMI reads flagged for high consumption as the dominant driver of estimate substitution for this subset, not missing manual field reads from route-completion/staffing lateness.

E-11 shows meter firmware v4.2 (rolled out 2026-06) reports register readings in units of "0.1 m3" while firmware v3.x reports in plain "m3" — a factor-of-10 unit difference between firmware generations on the same AMI network. release_summary.summary: The requester (SH-CS) originally framed the problem as a response-speed issue needing an auto-answering AI agent (CL-01), but that framing was rejected on evidence (E-01, E-02, E-03). Investigation first attributed the dispute surge's ESTIMATED-read bills to field-staffing/route lateness (PD-1@v1), but E-10 invalidated that: the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills (E-02) are entirely AMI-channel, and 1184 of them (95.5%) were valid AMI reads rejected as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION by billing rule BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01, no unit scaling, E-12), because meter firmware v4.2 reports in 0.1 m³ units that BV-17 misreads as whole m³, inflating apparent consumption ~10x (E-11). This became the current problem definition PD-1@v2, which passed the DEFINE Gate with CONDITIONAL_PASS. The release delivers two items within scope: a recommended BV-17 unit-conversion fix to billing engineering (SR-R-BV17-UNIT-FIX) and a dispute-volume trend monitoring deliverable from existing CRM data. The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION because two separate, more invasive verification steps (confirming the account-level BV-17 false-positive rate, and investigating the still-unexplained 1785 ACTUAL-read disputed bills, 59% of all disputes) remain open as verification obligations whose blocking scope lies outside what was actually released. No automated bill writes were made or proposed, consistent with the no-auto-bill-write constraint (K-BILLWRITE).
key_points: The initial request (CL-01, from SH-CS) asked for an AI agent to auto-answer dispute tickets and auto-fix wrong bills. This framing was tested as hypothesis H-RESPONSE-SPEED-FRAMING and REJECTED: CRM response times are within SLA (E-03) and the surge/split in read-type is not explained by response speed (E-01, E-02), so the problem was redefined rather than taken at face value.

The problem went through two versions. PD-1@v1 attributed the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills to manual-read route lateness/staffing (E-01, E-07), but new evidence E-10 showed those 1240 bills are entirely AMI-channel, invalidating that theory (dependency review DR-1; hypotheses H-FIELD-READ-HANDOFF-FAILURE and H-FIELD-STAFFING-SHORTFALL REJECTED).

The current problem (PD-1@v2) establishes that 1184 of the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills (95.5%) were valid AMI reads rejected as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION (E-10), caused by billing rule BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01, no unit_scaling, E-12) misreading v4.2 firmware's 0.1 m³ units as whole m³ (E-11), inflating apparent consumption ~10x (hypotheses H-BILLING-HIGH-CONSUMPTION-REJ, H-BV17-NO-SCALING, H-AMI-FIRMWARE-UNIT-MISMATCH all SUPPORTED/CONFIRMED).

The 1785 ACTUAL-read disputed bills (59% of all 3025 disputes, E-02) remain unexplained by this mechanism and are a separate open question (U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-CAUSE / VOB-U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-CAUSE, CRITICAL).

The DEFINE gate for PD-1 returned CONDITIONAL_PASS, with the unresolved ACTUAL-read cause and the unconfirmed BV-17 account-level false-positive rate deferred as verification obligations (VOB-U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-CAUSE, VOB-U-BV17-FALSE-POSITIVE-RATE) rather than blocking definition.

What was released (solution design SD-2, release scope): a recommendation to SH-BILL/billing engineering to add firmware-aware unit conversion to BV-17 (SR-R-BV17-UNIT-FIX, action recommend_billing_rule_fix on DA-RULES), and a dispute-volume trend monitoring deliverable from existing CRM data (action monitor_dispute_volume_trend on DA-TICKET, using E-05/M-DISPUTE-VOLUME).

The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION: the two open verification obligations (ACTUAL-read cause, BV-17 false-positive rate) have blocking_scope outside the actual release scope, so per the stated inputs they did not block this narrower release; they are instead logged as known limitations.

No automated bill writes occurred or were proposed: K-BILLWRITE requires Billing Operations (SH-BILL) authority for any bill adjustment/credit, and the released scope is limited to a recommendation plus a monitoring deliverable, consistent with SC-NO-AUTO-BILL-WRITE.
limitations_explained: The cause of the 1785 ACTUAL-read disputed bills (59% of all 3025 disputes) is still unestablished this cycle; the BV-17 unit-scaling finding only explains the ESTIMATED-read subset, not these. This is tracked as open CRITICAL verification obligation VOB-U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-CAUSE, whose blocking_scope (investigate_actual_read_dispute_cause, investigate_billing_rule_change_log) falls outside this release's scope.

The BV-17 account-level false-positive rate was not confirmed: the deterministic check (quantify_bv17_affected_account_impact against DA-BILL) that would verify the 1184 REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION reads are unit-mismatch false positives (rather than genuine high consumption) was withheld because open HIGH-impact VOB-U-BV17-FALSE-POSITIVE-RATE is unresolved; this blocking_scope is also outside release scope.

Within contest execution authority, there is no way to verify that the recommended BV-17 unit-conversion fix (SR-R-BV17-UNIT-FIX) is actually deployed by billing engineering, nor to observe its post-deployment effect on disputes or rejection rates.

The DEFINE Gate for the current problem definition (PD-1) returned only a CONDITIONAL_PASS, meaning some review items were deferred as tracked verification obligations (VOBs) rather than fully resolved before definition closed.

Several assumptions underlying the earlier (now superseded) explanation remain only partially settled in the record: A-STAFFING-ROOT-CAUSE is still ACTIVE even though the staffing hypothesis it supports (H-FIELD-STAFFING-SHORTFALL) was REJECTED by E-10, and A-BV17-FALSE-POSITIVE and A-DISPUTE-LINKAGE-ESTIMATED remain ACTIVE, unverified assumptions pending the account-level cross-check and CRM reason-code review respectively.

exported_to_billing=true for 1184 of 1240 records shows the AMI read was successfully delivered/exported from MDMS; the failure occurred at billing import rejection, not at AMI data delivery, reinforcing this hypothesis's existing REJECTED status.

The current problem (PD-1@v2) establishes that 1184 of the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills (95.5%) were valid AMI reads rejected as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION (E-10), caused by billing rule BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01, no unit_scaling, E-12) misreading v4.2 firmware's 0.1 m³ units as whole m³ (E-11), inflating apparent consumption ~10x (hypotheses H-BILLING-HIGH-CONSUMPTION-REJ, H-BV17-NO-SCALING, H-AMI-FIRMWARE-UNIT-MISMATCH all SUPPORTED/CONFIRMED).
